chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), he said:
I asked him about (hunting by) killing with the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? So he said: No.

key_terms.الْبُنْدُقِ: pellet or ball-shaped projectile used as a projectile weapon, analogous to a lead ball or clay pellet; here referring to a blunt projectile that kills by impact rather than cutting
key_terms.الْحَجَرِ: stone used as a thrown weapon; since it kills by blunt force rather than by a cutting edge, prey killed by it is not considered lawfully slaughtered
key_terms.قَتْلِ: killing/slaying; in the context of hunting (sayd), the manner of killing determines whether the game is halal or haram

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible (halal) to eat prey killed by throwing a stone or pellet in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith records a jurisprudential ruling on the permissibility of consuming game killed by a thrown stone or pellet. Muhammad ibn Muslim asks one of the two Imams (either al-Baqir or al-Sadiq, peace be upon them) whether prey killed in this manner is lawful to eat. The Imam's categorical answer is 'No,' establishing that only prey killed by a weapon with a cutting edge (like an arrow) or by trained hunting animals is permissible — blunt projectiles like stones and pellets do not meet the Islamic requirements for lawful slaughter during hunting.
